feature: QUIC ordered sent-packet tracking without monotonic exact-index writes

implementation: Strictly increasing sent packet numbers keep ordered packet metadata without allocating or writing the best-effort exact-index hash. Tail and binary-search lookup remain exact; unordered synthetic history retains sparse hash indexing plus the linear fallback and exact duplicate checks even when a candidate is above the unordered tail.
Cumulative ACK coverage proves full retained-history bounds from the first and last packet before falling back to lower/upper binary searches for partial ranges.

Ordered recovery queues with no retransmission copies retire packet-count and payload-byte aggregates once per ACK instead of repeating saturating counter updates for every acknowledged entry. The hot applyAck entry is 32-byte aligned to make its instruction placement independent of unrelated packet-space code size.
The first server 1-RTT send now requires three durable-ownership allocations instead of four.

quiche.observation: Recovery keeps sent packets in ordered VecDeque storage and appends ordinary sends at the tail.

tquic.observation: Each packet-number space keeps ordered VecDeque sent metadata and merges ascending ACK ranges with an ascending sent-packet cursor.

ack.note: The 100000-cycle decision binaries changed only the identical benchmark constant in temporary baseline/candidate worktrees. The source change and temporary worktree were removed after capture.

sent_ack_validation_ns_per_op_median.interpretation: The repeated invariant cumulative-ACK check fell below the benchmark's integer-nanosecond reporting resolution. This is retained as a no-regression sentinel, not an exact universal latency claim.

ack_recovery_100k.recovery_interpretation: The longer recovery timer passes after aligning the hot applyAck entry: arm medians favor the candidate by 3.07%, paired median favors it by 2.49%, and wins are mixed at 3/5. This is retained as a no-regression gate rather than a broad recovery speed claim.

initial_ack_regression.observation: Hash-write removal alone moved the 4096-packet cumulative ACK validation median from 28 to 32 ns/op, so it was not accepted without the endpoint-bound coverage fast path.

short_recovery_timer.resolution: The 25 ms recovery arm was too short to decide a sub-2% boundary. The otherwise identical 100000-cycle arm above runs about 20 times longer and replaces it for the acceptance decision.

recovery_profile.observation: Cycles sampling showed lower candidate self attribution in Queue.applyAck and Queue.recycleEntry while much of the benchmark remained inlined into main. It is diagnostic support only; the long fixed-binary timer is the decision gate.

unaligned_unordered_duplicate_layout.resolution: The unordered-duplicate correctness fix shifted byte-identical Queue.applyAck code by 16 bytes and exposed a stable instruction-placement regression. Aligning this hot public method to 32 bytes produced the accepted decision row above.

development_guards.rejected_empty_retransmission_deinit_ski: A follow-up branch that skipped deinit for never-grown retransmission storage regressed the single recovery smoke and was removed before final measurement.

verification.focused_debug: sent-packet coverage, packet tracker, and recovery filters passed
verification.real_h3: three final-source 4-stream 16-MiB TLS/H3 uploads from netz to quic-go completed 48 MiB total at 168.534-170.380 MiB/s; the reverse role also completed all three exact-byte/checksum/FIN samples
verification.quic_go_http3: QUIC v1/v2 bidirectional cancellation, dropped STOP_SENDING recovery, trailers, redirect/pool reuse, and informational response matrices passed
verification.quic_go_loss_reorder: 32/64-stream mixed FIN/reset churn passed for both endpoint-role pairs, both sender roles, loss and reordering, two runs per arm
verification.tquic: HTTP/3 normal, Retry, connection reuse, and two-phase GOAWAY passed in both endpoint-role directions

scope: The microbenchmark and real-H3 evidence are same-application-shape. They do not establish equal-wire superiority over another implementation.
remaining_gap: Packet protection, equal-wire HTTP/3 packetization, and shared-socket event-loop scheduling remain broader performance targets.
